cards.title: Main request · declare an incident
items: 1. CreateIncidentModal sends POST /api/incidents with the session cookie. The API verifies the JWT and current workspace membership; viewers cannot write.
2. server.ts:327–385 validates input and optional service ownership, commits incidents + incident_events together, then reads the created incident and returns HTTP 201.

3–6. After commit, broadcast() publishes a small PostgreSQL notification. Each API listener fans it out to that organization's SSE clients. ProductApp refreshes records after an event (350 ms debounce).
The 201 response and asynchronous notification are separate outcomes. A notification-query failure falls back to clients attached to that process; SSE is not a durable replay queue.

cards.title: Runtime and persistence
items: Express routes, auth.ts, workspace.ts, ai.ts, monitor.ts and realtime.ts run inside the same Node process; they are logical modules, not independently deployed services (server.ts:828–843).
database.ts:4–65 owns the pg pool (max 10) and BEGIN/COMMIT/ROLLBACK helper. Route handlers and monitor.ts issue their own SQL through it.
backend/schema.sql stores organizations, users, memberships, services, checks, incidents, timeline events, AI analyses, telemetry and workspace invites.
workspace.ts:9–165 adds workspace switching, team permissions, notes and assignment through the same API, database and broadcast path.

cards.title: Signals and behavior-changing conditions
items: The monitor selects due, enabled services with health URLs; up to 25 per cycle, three concurrent checks. A service-row lock serializes probes. Two failures mark down and create an incident if none is active; recovery resolves health-monitor incidents.
Check now requires an authenticated non-viewer but bypasses the scheduled enabled/due test. Probes validate public DNS addresses and pin the HTTP(S) connection (security.ts:17–60).

Ingest bypasses cookie authentication but validates x-ingest-key, including under a row lock. Critical telemetry creates or updates an active telemetry-ingest incident; other severities only persist telemetry (server.ts:683–792).

cards.title: AI is an optional request branch
items: POST /api/incidents/:id/analyze reads incident, timeline, checks and telemetry. An unchanged context hash returns the saved analysis without a provider call (server.ts:429–475).

On a cache miss, ai.ts:93–211 requires an API key, sends evidence to OpenRouter, attempts at most two configured models and validates the structured result. The API persists analysis + timeline event and broadcasts completion.
If the provider fails, the API returns a marked stale saved analysis when available; otherwise the request errors. The deployed key and model availability were not inspected.

cards.title: Evidence scope and unknowns
items: Source-backed runtime overview at f1a3eb2. Node source references link to the pinned commit. Arrow labels describe observed calls; external senders and health targets are contracts, with actual deployments unknown.

api.ts:22–34 supports VITE_API_URL or same-origin /api. vite.config.ts:10–12 proxies development traffic to localhost:8787. vercel.json:3–7 configures an HTTPS rewrite to Railway; whether that deployment is active is unverified.

PostgreSQL is required. Neon is supported by the listener's pooler-host rewrite, but the deployed database host and replica count are unknown. UI decoration, build tooling and individual CRUD endpoints are grouped rather than expanded.
Existing uncommitted frontend/package-lock.json changes were excluded from source evidence. No application code was changed to create this diagram.
